lines.t: Karma helps DAOs track, quantify, and reward member contributions through an
integrated scoring system, giving visibility to active contributors across multiple
Karma is a platform that helps Decentralized Autonomous Organizations (DAOs) build and
maintain better communities by valuing and rewarding their members contributions. With a
scoring system called Karma Score, the platform integrates data from multiple DAO sources to
provide visibility, compensation, and recognition for active contributors.

At this step, I started by understanding DAOs and how Karma works in the context of Web3 communities. I conducted desk
research on popular DAO platforms such as Snapshot, Tally, and Twitter Community, and analyzed how member contributions
are typically tracked and rewarded. I also studied competitors and similar tools to understand industry standards and look for
opportunities for improvement. These findings helped build an initial understanding of user pain points, such as the lack of
transparency, rewards, and visibility for DAO contributors.
In the ideation step, I focused on designing an interface that displays DAO contributions in a comprehensive and easy to
understand way. The top priority was to display contribution metrics per DAO so that users can see how they are performing in
each community, while considering explorative features and filtering so that users can access the information that is most
relevant to them. I also developed a simple user journey to map out the flow of users as they browse through their contributions
Once the initial ideas were validated internally, 1 proceeded to create a high fidelity Ul design in Figma. I chose a modern, clean,
and professional visual style to reflect the blockchain world while remaining user friendly. I designed pages such as the
homepage and feature section with accessibility and visual consistency in mind.
To test the feasibility and ease of use of the design, I developed simple scenarios and tasks as the basis for usability testing.
These tests were designed to validate whether users could easily understand the information structure, navigate the platform,
and capture value from the Karma Score system.
In the beginning phase of the project, I conducted an in depth exploration to understand the context of the DAO ecosystem and the
needs of its users. This process included competitor analysis to see how other platforms showcase contributions and manage DAO
communities, identification of contributors' pain points regarding the lack of visibility and proper recognition of their contributions,
as well as mapping the key target users and audience consisting of active contributors and DAO community managers. These three
elements became the foundation for formulating a relevant, functional and user centered design approach.

This section illustrates the typical experience of a content creator using the app, from finding potential collaborators to completing
the journey and sharing content. Based on the pain points identified through competitor analysis, this journey highlights real user
frustrations and expectations, helping to shape features that prioritize safety, trust, and seamless collaboration.
An active DAO contributor who frequently votes, discusses, and submits proposals wants to feel
like his contributions are valued and visible in the community.
Contributors expect a transparent, integrated, and fair system for assessing contributions, as well
as a decent reward for their participation in various DAOs.
After identifying the contributors' lack of visibility and recognition across decentralized communities, I focused on crafting core
features that bring transparency, credibility, and rewards to their efforts. The goal was to design an experience that is intuitive,
trustworthy, and empowers users to track and showcase their impact across DAOs.

This section features a strong combination of bold headlines, informative subheadlines, and product preview visuals. The headline
"Build and Maintain Better Communities" uses large typography and graduating colors to highlight the keyword Better Communities,
indicating the main focus of the product. The subheadline provides context on how the platform works, which is to help DAOS
(Decentralized Autonomous Organizations) by defining and measuring contributions through a score called Karma Score.
The two CTA buttons ("Explore" and "Become a Member") come with a strong color contrast (green and black) to draw the user's
attention to explore or sign up right away. Underneath, a browser illustration shows the user's profile view within the platform, giving
an initial idea of the site's functionality, such as contribution scoring on various DAOs.
Overall, this section aims to attract attention, explain the main value, and invite users to take action right away.

This section is designed to visually and concisely explain how the contribution score called Karma Score is calculated. The design is
divided into two parts: the left side presents a text explanation of the Karma Score definition, while the right side displays the
contribution points in the form of large, striking green numbers. Each point is packaged in a card with a white background and
rounded corners, highlighting each activity that contributes to the score, such as voting, making proposals, and discussing.
Its function is to educate users, especially DAO contributors on how their activities are assessed and rewarded in the system. This
creates transparency and encourages more active engagement, as users can see first-hand how their actions impact their
reputation or score within the DAO community. This section also strengthens users' trust in the system used by the platform.
This section features the three key figures behind the Karma platform, aligned in neat and professional individual cards. Each card
features a photo of the team member against a green background that matches the color theme, their name in bold typography, and
their job title in smaller, lighter text.
The idea of this section is to build user trust in the credibility and leadership behind Karma. By presenting the faces of the founders
and core team, users can feel the personal side of the platform they are using, and understand that the product is developed by
experienced and dedicated individuals. The clean, consistent and professional visual approach also reinforces Karma's brand image
as a serious and trusted platform.

Through this visual, users can understand that Karma Score plays an important role in supporting individual development within the
DAO community. Contributors can improve the quality of their work based on measurable metrics, prove their contributions to open
new opportunities, and be more easily discovered by others based on the score they have built. This section serves not only as
information, but also as a motivational boost to more actively and consistently contribute to the DAO ecosystem. The minimalist yet
informative visual style reinforces the main message effectively.
This section aims to showcase the credibility and support it has gained from various DAO communities with the title "Supported
DAOs". The design features the large text "SUPPORT" as a background that forms a solid and inclusive impression, while in the
center is the bold text "Supported DAOs" to emphasize the context. The logos of the supported DAOs are displayed in two rows with
a uniform and professional look, reinforcing the message that the platform is trusted by many. The soft background color gradation
and decorative elements in the bottom right corner give a modern and clean feel without distracting from the main focus. This
section effectively builds trust with new users through a clean look and visual evidence of support.

To evaluate the effectiveness and usability of Karma, I conducted usability testing sessions by setting up realistic scenarios with
task based activities. The main objective of the testing was to understand how users interact with the application, identify pain
points, and validate whether the designed features are truly aligned with the needs and expectations of DAO community users.
Participants were given the following scenario to complete:
1. You are a member of multiple DAOs and want to check your Karma score and activity in each DAO. How do you check it?
2. You want to explore more information about the DAOs you contribute to. What should you do to get that information?
3. You want to share your contribution profile with your network. How to share it?
4. You are only interested in your Snapshot contributions. What should you do?
